name: Shape Odd One Out
blurb: All but one of these shapes share something. Find the one that does not.
childIntro: Look at all the shapes. Most of them are alike in one way. Which one is different?
howItWorks: The child marks the figure that does not belong. On OLSAT this runs at levels A through D, so kindergarten to third grade, and then stops. The rule can be about shape, count, shading, orientation or an abstract property like the number of corners.
parentTip: Have your child say what the others have in common before naming the odd one out. If they cannot finish the sentence they are all ___, they are guessing. This is also the quickest question type to practice with buttons or coins on a table.
